items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Russell Jacquet, and Mohawk, the bass player. I can’t think of his name. We used to call him Mohawk. And Shadow Wilson on drums. He had just a fantastic band. Sir Charles Thompson I think was on piano. He was such a big name, ’til he was playing all the top places that there were to play. There was one outfit – one working gimmick which they called T.O.B.A. – Theatrical Booking Act, Association, or something [Theater Owners’ Booking Association]. But we used to have a nickname for it: Tough on Black Actors. In…
In your mind, why didn’t the George Hudson band go to the next level?
